trust_decision.summary: PswRecovery.doGet accepts any valid PSW_RECOVERY ticket and then resets the password of the account named by the separate client-supplied userId parameter, never checking that the ticket was issued to that user; the fix adds ticket.getUserId() == userId to the ticket check.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the PswRecovery ticket; the servlet of the same name holds the only consumer of PSW_RECOVERY tickets, and the ticket-type check is the obvious place to add the binding.

fix_sites.module_kind: web servlet (same module as the ticket producer LoginServiceImpl.resetPassword)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site and no qualifying O8 route. The only adjacent unbound value is the 'tenant' request parameter (PswRecovery.java:74-76), which a solver could dismiss because it picks only the password policy and SMTP sender, not which account gets reset.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The legitimate recovery link carries the ticket owner's own userId and must still reset that user's password and send the psw.rec1 mail. The ticket is single-use: it is disabled on first use and checked through isTicketExpired.

O6_input_shapes: ticketId fallback from a request attribute (PswRecovery.java:78-80)
ticketId fallback from a session attribute (PswRecovery.java:82-84)
userId as a decimal string, parsed once to long and compared to the ticket's userId (fix.diff:196, fix.diff:214)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The 'tenant' parameter is taken from the request and not bound to ticket.getTenantId(); a variant that resolves the user by (tenant, username) would make tenant identity part of the account choice.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Tickets already store tenantId (LoginServiceImpl.java:115), and multi-tenant lookups are common elsewhere in the code, so a maintainer could plausibly resolve the user per tenant here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second ticket consumer (for example a REST or SOAP password-recovery endpoint in logicaldoc-webservice) that redeems a PSW_RECOVERY ticket against a caller-supplied user id or username.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The webservice module already exposes user and password operations (logicaldoc-webservice/src/main/java/com/logicaldoc/webservice/soap/endpoint/SoapSecurityService.java:312). This is a WHERE-type plant only, so it counts as an extra.

O9_family: authentication / weak password recovery (CWE-640): recovery token not bound to the account it resets

O10_build.toolchain: Maven multi-module; Java 21 (logicaldoc-parent/pom.xml:14); GWT gui module at source level 17 (logicaldoc-parent/pom.xml:16)
O10_build.project_tests: No PswRecovery or LoginServiceImpl tests exist (no logicaldoc-webapp/src/test/java/com/logicaldoc/web/*Test.java). Related: logicaldoc-webapp/src/test/java/com/logicaldoc/web/service/SecurityServiceImplTest.java and logicaldoc-core/src/test/java/com/logicaldoc/core/ticket/HibernateTicketDAOTest.java. The fix adds no tests.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add ticket.getUserId() == userId to the check at PswRecovery.java:91, or ignore the userId parameter and use ticket.getUserId(). Both are correct; the obvious fix is also the full fix.

out_of_scope_notes: LoginServiceImpl.changePassword (logicaldoc-webapp/src/main/java/com/logicaldoc/web/service/LoginServiceImpl.java:57-59) is a login-screen RPC that passes the caller's userId as requestor; SecurityServiceImpl.changePassword skips the old-password check when oldPassword is null (logicaldoc-webapp/src/main/java/com/logicaldoc/web/service/SecurityServiceImpl.java:327-341). This is a separate weakness (no ticket involved) and was not pursued.
LoginServiceImpl.resetPassword reveals whether a username exists through distinct error messages (LoginServiceImpl.java:105-106, 171-172); this is user enumeration and was not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell size check within the limits).
offline_after_build not confirmed; the servlet sends mail through EMailSender (PswRecovery.java:162-163), which tests would need to mock or stub.
Whether any servlet filter in web.xml restricts /pswrecovery was not checked; it is mapped at logicaldoc-webapp/src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml:789-791 with no session check inside the servlet.

Whether HibernateTicketDAO.findByTicketId's validate listeners (logicaldoc-core/src/main/java/com/logicaldoc/core/ticket/HibernateTicketDAO.java:141-142) add any user or tenant check was not traced; it is assumed they do not, given the advisory.
